audit.title: Chainlink Data Feeds
audit.summary: This is a well-structured conceptual hub for Chainlink Data Feeds: clean heading hierarchy (18 headings, 0 level skips, median 86-word sections), a strong opening definition, and 6 primary-source links. Its biggest GEO strength is answer-first extractability and citation density; its biggest opportunity is machine-readability (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dated freshness signal in the served HTML) combined with vague quantifiers ("several hours," "some heartbeats") where concrete numbers would lift both credibility and extractability. Honest verdict: a solid, retrievable overview page that would move into Strong territory with a feed-comparison table, concrete threshold numbers, and structured metadata.

recommendations.title: Add a feed-types comparison table
recommendations.issue: seven feed types presented only as a bullet link list; 0 tables on page.
recommendations.change: add a table with columns Feed type · Data returned · Typical use case · Addresses page link, one row per feed (Price, SmartData, MVR, SVR, Rate/Volatility, L2 sequencer, Self-managed).
recommendations.why: engines lift tables as self-contained comparison units and can build justified "which feed should I use" answers.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with concrete threshold numbers
recommendations.where: "### Check the timestamp of the latest answer"
recommendations.issue: "Some heartbeats are configured to last several hours"
recommendations.change: give a concrete example, e.g. "Heartbeats range from ~27 seconds to 24 hours depending on the feed; e.g. ETH/USD on Ethereum updates on a 3600-second heartbeat or a 0.5% deviation." Cite the addresses page for the source values.
recommendations.why: quantitative claims with units are among the highest-lift changes; the page currently reports 0 numerals with units.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema, canonical URL, and dateModified
recommendations.issue: measured 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about` (Chainlink Data Feeds), and a `<link rel="canonical">` to `https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds`.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and visible freshness raise agent parseability and E-E-A-T trust.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased subheadings under Monitoring
recommendations.issue: concept-titled headings; no coverage of how devs query ("stale price," "latestRoundData old timestamp").
recommendations.change: add H3s phrased as questions: "How do I detect a stale price feed?" and "Why is `latestRoundData()` returning an old `updatedAt`?" answering with the existing heartbeat/timestamp guidance.
recommendations.why: symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical one-line definition to the Price Feeds section
recommendations.issue: opens with "Smart contracts often act in real-time on data such as prices of assets" — context, not a definition.
recommendations.change: lead with "Chainlink Price Feeds are decentralized oracle feeds that publish aggregated asset prices onchain for consumption via the `AggregatorV3Interface`."
recommendations.why: a crisp lead sentence gives engines a verbatim-liftable definition and defends against parametric substitution.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal runnable read example
recommendations.issue: names `latestRoundData()` and `AggregatorV3Interface` but shows 0 code blocks.
recommendations.change: add a short language-tagged Solidity snippet with the import and a `latestRoundData()` call, or link inline to the exact guide snippet. Lead with the canonical helper, not a generic web3 call.
recommendations.why: copy-pasteable, imported snippets are cited by coding agents; naming the SDK interface first resists generic-idiom substitution.

recommendations.title: Name the "call the aggregator directly" anti-pattern as an explicit Don't
recommendations.issue: "You can call the `latestRoundData()` function directly on the aggregator, but it is a best practice to use the proxy"
recommendations.change: restructure as a bold Do/Don't: "**Do** read through the proxy contract. **Don't** call `latestRoundData()` on the aggregator directly — it breaks when the aggregator is upgraded."
recommendations.why: explicit Don'ts prevent engines from lifting the tempting-wrong pattern out of context.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers where numbers belong: "several hours," "some aggregators," "several others" (measured: many/several/various/some/most present). Not stuffing — just imprecision that underperforms.
No dated freshness signal (dateModified absent) on a page that explicitly discusses time-sensitive updates and migrations.
No walls of prose, no broken cross-references, no keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff beyond one contact callout.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; ensure this page is listed in it.
Site-level JSON-LD / canonical templating and a freshness-cadence policy are best fixed at the docs-platform level, not per page.
Head metadata could not be verified from the served content; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` so schema/canonical/date presence can be confirmed rather than inferred.
